content:
Since the iPhone 4 bumper case was first released, the iPhone bumper case has always been very popular, but the available styles are now quite limited. If you're looking for a minimalist protective case, Rhinoshield is a decent option.

Last year, Apple finally returned to the bumper case market with the iPhone Air bumper. I had hoped Apple would extend their bumper case to the iPhone 18 Pro (just as they did with the iPhone 11 clear case back then), but unfortunately they didn't. While searching for alternatives, I came across Rhinoshield's Minimalist Impact Bumper case.

Key Details

The fit of the Impact Bumper is similar to most other bumper cases — the lip around the screen is relatively small, while the rear edge is slightly larger. The case has a unique design that I quite like: it features a special support point that keeps the camera plateau and lenses from directly contacting the surface the phone is placed on, which is especially important for the 17 Pro and 18 Pro with their aluminium bodies. Compared to a typical bumper case, this one offers significantly more protection. It also eliminates the annoying wobble when using the phone on a flat surface.

That said, the fit of the case isn't quite what I wanted. It feels a little loose when fitted, and the edges flex outward quite easily, so I'm a bit concerned it may become looser over time. Even so, I don't think the phone would fly out of the case if dropped (I've inadvertently already tested this). That said, the entire case is made of hard plastic rather than rubber, so hopefully it'll hold up in the long run. Rhinoshield says the case is made from just one material, making it 100% recyclable.

The case comes in three colours designed to complement the iPhone 18 Pro: white, blue, and black (sorry, fans of the dark red colour are out of luck). I have the blue version, which is close to Glacier but not an exact match.

Cons

However, there are some drawbacks. The thing I'm least happy about with this case is that the buttons are quite hard to press. For some reason they chose a nearly flush design, and combined with how the buttons are constructed, the result is a soft, mushy feel when pressing them.

The overall choice of material can also be considered a drawback. To me, it feels cheaper in the hand than Apple's iPhone Air bumper, though some may prefer this texture. I definitely prefer it over the typical TPU/rubber clear case material. However, this material combined with the loose-fitting design seems to easily attract pocket lint.

If you use Apple's Wrist Strap or Crossbody Strap, note that this case lacks the necessary attachment points for a lanyard.

Conclusion

Rhinoshield's bumper case is far from perfect, and I still wish Apple would extend their bumper case to other iPhone models. But in the end, I decided to keep this case, mainly because it gives me a near-naked-phone experience while not having to worry about the fragile aluminium frame getting scratched or dented. As far as I know, the bumper case is generally only available on their own website, costing around US$30 with shipping — roughly the same price as Apple's bumper case (US$39). You can buy the Rhinoshield Minimalist Impact Bumper case here. (Amazon listings do pop up from time to time, so you can try searching there too.)
